story.title: Russia, Ukraine, and US Begin Peace Talks in Abu Dhabi
story.summary: Three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States commenced on November 10 in Abu Dhabi, marking the first such meeting since February. The discussions aim to address future security guarantees and seek to end the ongoing conflict that began nearly five years ago with Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground during the talks?
explore_lenses.title: Fighting and civilian harm continued
explore_lenses.summary: The Abu Dhabi session opened amid continuing long-range attacks rather than an observable battlefield pause. UN reporting indicates that civilians remain exposed to escalating attacks even as diplomats pursue a political track.

claims.text: Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 162 drones and a ballistic missile overnight; Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 155 Ukrainian drones over eight Russian regions and Crimea. These are wartime claims by the respective sides and were not independently verified in the report.

The UN said civilian casualties in Ukraine were reaching record highs amid escalating attacks; it cited a reported Ukrainian civilian death from a drone attack in Russia’s Kursk region the day before its November 9 briefing.
The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission said that, before the November 2 attack in Komyshuvakha, aerial glide bombs had killed at least 478 civilians and injured 2,667 in Ukraine during 2026.

explore_lenses.label: Why did diplomacy return to Abu Dhabi now?
explore_lenses.title: A stalled process was restarted
explore_lenses.summary: The meeting resumes a U.S.-mediated trilateral process that had previously failed to produce a visible breakthrough. The immediate agenda has narrowed around security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures.

claims.text: The Congressional Research Service says the first 2026 trilateral meeting was held in Abu Dhabi in January, while formal Russia-Ukraine talks did not resume after U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran began in late February.
Associated Press reported that the November 10 session was the first U.S.-mediated three-way meeting since February and that three earlier rounds this year had not produced significant breakthroughs.

Ukraine’s president said Kyiv would propose de-escalatory steps and seeks an understanding on arranging a leaders-level trilateral meeting; he also identified security guarantees and postwar recovery resources as necessary elements of a settlement.
Russia regards NATO as a threat, while Ukraine seeks arrangements meant to prevent another Russian invasion, according to AP’s account of the competing security concerns.

explore_lenses.label: What are the next confirmed diplomatic steps?
explore_lenses.title: The talks were scheduled for a second day
explore_lenses.summary: The confirmed immediate step is continuation of the Abu Dhabi meeting on November 11. A leaders-level meeting remains a Ukrainian objective, not an announced outcome.

claims.text: The UAE Foreign Ministry confirmed that the third round of U.S.-Russia-Ukraine trilateral talks launched in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and described its purpose as supporting dialogue toward a political solution.
Reporting ahead of the meeting described the Abu Dhabi session as a two-day gathering, scheduled for November 10-11.

Ukraine’s stated priorities include security guarantees, an energy ceasefire, Black Sea access, expanded prisoner exchanges and preparations for a leaders-level meeting involving Ukraine, the United States and Russia.
Forecast: The UAE foreign minister expressed hope that the talks would lead to practical steps toward ending the conflict; this was an aspiration, not a commitment by the negotiating parties.

story_report.summary: Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10, resuming three-way negotiations for the first time since February. The UAE said the third round of trilateral talks was intended to support dialogue toward a political solution, while reporting ahead of the session described a two-day meeting scheduled for November 10-11. The immediate outcome was the launch of discussions centered on future security guarantees, with no announced settlement or ceasefire.

sections.heading: Earlier Negotiations Produced No Breakthrough
sections.body: The November session followed an earlier trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi in January, according to the Congressional Research Service. Formal Russia-Ukraine talks did not resume after U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran began in late February, the service said. Associated Press reported that three previous rounds this year had not yielded significant breakthroughs, providing the backdrop for renewed negotiations.

sections.heading: Security Guarantees Define Core Differences
sections.body: Kyiv says a settlement requires security guarantees and postwar recovery resources, and plans to propose de-escalatory steps while seeking an understanding on a leaders-level trilateral meeting. Ukraine has also listed an energy ceasefire, Black Sea access and expanded prisoner exchanges among its priorities. Russia views NATO as a threat, while Ukraine seeks arrangements designed to prevent another Russian invasion, according to AP’s account of the competing concerns.

sections.heading: Fighting Continues During Negotiations
sections.body: No nationwide ceasefire or verified reduction in attacks was announced as the talks began. Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 162 drones and a ballistic missile overnight, while Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 155 Ukrainian drones over eight Russian regions and Crimea; those wartime claims were not independently verified. The UN has said civilian casualties in Ukraine were reaching record highs amid escalating attacks, and reported that glide bombs had killed at least 478 civilians and injured 2,667 in Ukraine during 2026 before a November 2 attack in Komyshuvakha.

unresolved.text: The proposed security-guarantee package, including enforcement mechanisms and possible European roles, has not been made public.
No joint communiqué, ceasefire agreement, timetable for further talks or date for a leaders-level meeting was confirmed in the consulted material.

related_stories.title: Iran Denies Ongoing Negotiations with the U.S. Amid Sanctions
related_stories.summary: Iran has stated that there are no negotiations currently taking place with the United States. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that economic sanctions and a naval blockade are effectively reducing the need for major combat operations against Iran. He communicated this position during discussions with G7 allies, asserting that the current strategy is working well.

related_stories.title: Novaya Gazeta, Russia's Last Major Independent Newspaper, Shuts Down Amid Government Pressure
related_stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, the last major independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, has closed its office after over 30 years of operation. The closure is attributed to increasing government pressure and a crackdown on free press in Russia. Journalists from the outlet noted that the process of silencing independent media has been ongoing for many years.

related_stories.title: Hegseth Responds Defiantly to Impeachment Efforts
related_stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has dismissed the impeachment effort initiated by Republican Congressman Thomas Massie as a 'farce' and a 'political stunt.' Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, citing alleged violations related to the Iran war and other military actions. Hegseth defended his record during a press briefing, asserting that the impeachment attempt is driven by policy disagreements rather than legitimate high crimes.

related_stories.title: Teddy Riner Announces Presidential Bid in France
related_stories.summary: Teddy Riner, the 37-year-old Olympic judo champion, has declared his candidacy for the French presidency in the 2027 election. He made the announcement via social media, amid a political landscape where public opinion is divided between far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon and far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.
